scope: Fact-check of heat treatment and surface treatment cards: lecture-9-heat-treatment, lecture-10-surface-treatment, heat/surface-related self-miscellanea cards, and visible Heat Treatment section cards in scope.
summary: Checked 93 cards against Lecture 9, Lecture 10, the miscellanea/self-assessment prompts, selected past-exam wording, and matching notes pages. I found no critical wrong-answer issues and no major misleading theory issues. The issues below are minor option/source cleanup items.

issues.problem: Option B is malformed as "200 MPa A". The correct answer and calculation are still clear, but the extra letter makes the distractor look like a data-entry artifact.
issues.sourceEvidence: The card uses the steel estimate UTS(MPa) approximately 3.3 x HV; 420 HV gives about 1386 MPa, so 1400 MPa is the intended answer. This is supported by the card source TMM.txt and the mechanical-property context in slides&docs/Lecture 9 Steel Heat Treatment.pdf, page/slide 10.
issues.proposedFix: Change option B from "200 MPa A" to "200 MPa".

issues.problem: The explanation relies on nitriding, but the source citation points to Lecture 10 page 1, which is the carburizing slide. The nitriding evidence is on page 2.
issues.sourceEvidence: slides&docs/Lecture 10 Thermal Chemical Treatment of Steels.pdf, page/slide 2 lists nitriding applications including high wear parts and high localized loaded parts, and gives nitriding as an extremely hard surface/tough-core process.
issues.proposedFix: Update the source to cite slides&docs/Lecture 10 Thermal Chemical Treatment of Steels.pdf, page/slide 2 in addition to the miscellanea prompt.

issues.problem: The source citation points to Lecture 10 page 1, but induction hardening is introduced and developed on pages/slides 5-7.
issues.sourceEvidence: slides&docs/Lecture 10 Thermal Chemical Treatment of Steels.pdf, pages/slides 5-7 show the induction hardening principle, current penetration depth, inductors, and hardness profiles. Notes-split/TMM NOTES BY PAST-YEAR STUDENTS_251222_110914-161-186.pdf, pages 1-2 add that induction hardening needs suitable starting steel/microstructure and does not add chemistry.
issues.proposedFix: Change the Lecture 10 source reference from page 1 to pages/slides 5-7; optionally add the matching notes page 1-2 citation.

issues.problem: The answer and explanation identify nitriding, but the source citation points to Lecture 10 page 1, while the nitriding process details are on page 2 and the low-distortion summary is on page 11.
issues.sourceEvidence: slides&docs/Lecture 10 Thermal Chemical Treatment of Steels.pdf, page/slide 2 describes nitriding below the carburizing section, and page/slide 11 lists nitriding distortion as minimum in the chemical surface-treatment summary.
issues.proposedFix: Update the source to cite Lecture 10 page/slide 2 and/or page/slide 11 rather than page 1.

uncertainties.note: The old past-exam wording "resist specific loads" has no answer key in PAST_EXAMS/QUESTIONS_SET_1.txt. Lecture 10 supports nitriding for high localized loaded parts, while course prompts also separately discuss point-load crushing and durable gear case layers. I did not mark the answer wrong because the lecture wording on nitriding supports the current choice, but the wording would benefit from a clearer source citation.

Lecture 9 page/slide 9 clearly states that CCT curves are shifted bottom-right relative to TTT curves and that incubation times in CCT are longer. One matching notes page says continuous-transformation incubation times are lower, apparently contradicting the slide. I treated the slide as authoritative per AGENTS.md, so the card was not flagged.
